front: What is Apache modules in one sentence?
back: Static (compiled-in) vs shared (dynamic LoadModule) — what you can toggle without recompiling httpd.

front: Explain the mental model of Apache modules (how the system thinks).
back: Apache httpd loads modules at startup. Static modules are baked into the binary — always present. Shared modules (.so) load via LoadModule in config. Only load what you need: fewer modules = smaller attack surface and memory.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Apache modules?
back: httpd binary → apache2ctl -M # Debian/Ubuntu → httpd -M # RHEL → apachectl -t -D DUMP_MODULES → sudo a2enmod rewrite ssl headers proxy proxy_http

front: Symptom: Invalid command 'RewriteRule' — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: mod_rewrite loaded? · Fix: a2enmod rewrite

front: Symptom: Apache won't start after enable — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: apachectl configtest · Fix: Fix LoadModule order; missing .so

front: Symptom: PHP works, static 403 — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Directory permissions · Fix: Require all granted + filesystem perms

front: Symptom: SSL handshake fail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: mod_ssl + cert paths · Fix: SSLEngine on; cert file readable

front: Symptom: Proxy 502 — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: mod_proxy enabled · Fix: a2enmod proxy proxy_http; backend up

front: Gotcha with Apache modules: what silently fails?
back: MPM switch — can't mix prefork/worker/event blindly; restart required; PHP-FPM pairs with event/worker. Module loaded twice — duplicate LoadModule lines break startup. Distro splits packages — libapache2-mod-* separate from core.

front: When should you NOT use Apache modules?
back: Don't enable mod_php on new stacks — use PHP-FPM + proxy_fcgi or Nginx. Don't load debug modules (mod_info, mod_status) on public-facing servers without IP restrict.
